questions.stem: Aster Ltd's plant is a CGU: building 400, machines 300, goodwill allocated 100, inventory 60 (Rs crore). FVLCS of the CGU is 690; value in use is 700. Machines have an individual FVLCS of 280 crore.

questions.q: The residual Rs 60 is allocated:
o: Pro rata (building 27.3, machines 20.5, inventory 4.1 — subject to floors; inventory cannot go below NRV so floors matter)
questions.why: Pro rata on carrying amounts with floors; the machines' floor at 280 binds only if pro-rata would push them below it — 300 − 20.5 = 279.5 < 280 ⇒ machines stop at 280 and the excess 0.5 reallocates to the building — the beauty spot of this case is the floor reallocation.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: floors block pro rata — the defining nuance Pro rata with a stop sign: no asset falls below its own dignity.
mem.link: Chapter 11 — Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements

questions.q: For basic EPS, weighted-average number of shares is adjusted for:
o: A bonus issue and a share split — by retrospective restatement of prior periods
Rights issue at full fair value
A fresh public issue at market price
Buy-back completed during the year only
questions.why: Bonus issues/splits/capitalisation issues are time-weighted from the beginning (retrospectively to the earliest period presented) since no consideration flows; rights issues use a correction factor = fair value per share / theoretical ex-rights price. New issues at fair value count from issue date.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — EPS mechanics with bonus-vs-rights distinction repeat constantly Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: EPS adjustment ladder: bonus/split = pure restatement; rights = FER/TERP factor; IPO = day count. TERP always drags price down.
mem.link: Ch 11

questions.q: An entity has 10% convertible debentures while its weighted-average borrowing rate is 6%. Effect on diluted EPS is:
o: Anti-dilutive — convertible profits less tax-adjusted interest exceed the added share capital's EPS effect
Dilutive only if converted before year-end
questions.why: If the assumed conversion increases EPS per share added (i.e., add-back interest net of tax divided by new shares exceeds basic EPS), conversion is anti-dilutive and excluded from diluted EPS.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — anti-dilution checks are the trap within the trap AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Dilution test: compute per-share effect of each instrument vs basic EPS. Positive? Exclude — diluted EPS only travels DOWN.
mem.link: Ch 11

questions.q: Recoverable amount under Ind AS 36 is:
o: Higher of FVLCS and value in use
Fair value less costs of disposal
Present value of pre-tax cash flows
questions.why: Recoverable amount = HIGHER of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use; impairment when CA > that. Value in use uses PRE-TAX cash flows and a pre-tax discount rate in Ind AS 36.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — recoverable-amount definition with tax nuance repeats Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Higher of the two exits (sell vs keep). CGU fails only if BOTH are below carrying — never on a single miss.
mem.link: Ch 11

questions.q: While estimating value in use, which of the following is EXCLUDED from future cash flows?
o: Cash outflows necessary for continuing use of the asset
Estimates of restructuring to which the entity is NOT yet committed
Taxes paid on operating cash flow at pre-tax rate basis
questions.why: VIU cash flows exclude restructuring commitments not yet made (only committed restructurings' benefits may be included), exclude financing and tax flows, and include expenditures to maintain the asset's current condition.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the not-yet-committed-restructuring exclusion is a classic distractor AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: No counting blessings from plans not yet done: uncommitted restructuring stays out; committed restructuring's savings come in.
mem.link: Ch 11

questions.q: Impairment of a CGU containing goodwill is allocated FIRST to:
questions.why: CGU impairment sequence: goodwill first (full stop), then other assets pro rata, never below the highest of FVLCS, VIU and zero.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the waterfall order is a guaranteed 1-marker AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Goodwill drinks first in the impairment waterfall — then pro rata floors (FV, VIU, 0) per asset.
mem.link: Ch 11 + Ch 12

questions.q: Under Ind AS 108, the quantitative thresholds for reportable segments use:
o: 10% of combined revenue, 10% of combined profit/loss, 10% of combined assets
questions.why: 10% tests: revenue (incl inter-segment), profit/loss (larger of absolute combined profit or loss), assets. Plus management-approach identification via CODM.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — threshold recall is a freebie that appears AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Segments report at 10% on three dials: revenue, bigger of profit/loss, assets — under CODM's watch.
mem.link: Ch 11

questions.q: Which item is NOT reclassified (recycled) to profit or loss subsequently?
o: Exchange differences on translating a foreign operation
Fair value on debt instrument at FVOCI
questions.why: Ind AS 1/19: DB-plan remeasurements stay in equity and are never recycled; the other options reclassify on disposal/settlement/realisation.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — recycle-vs-stay is the cleanest 2-marker of the chapter AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: Ind AS 1 — other comprehensive income
mem.tip: OCI items have passports: most eventually re-enter P&L (recycle); DB remeasurements and some equity FVOCI elections have no visa — they never return.
mem.link: Ch 11

questions.q: Capitalising borrowing costs, relative to expensing, initially:
o: Increases assets and defers expense — boosting current profit
questions.why: Capitalised interest becomes part of the asset: current expense lower ⇒ current profit higher; assets and debt both heavier (later depreciation higher).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — impact-direction questions are common Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Interest into the asset = today's profits prettier, tomorrow's depreciation heavier, ratios both ways.

questions.q: Judgments (not estimates) that management made in applying policies are disclosed:
o: In the notes, identifying the most critical judgments
In the auditor's report as the entity's own statement
questions.why: Ind AS 1 requires disclosure of judgments management made in applying accounting policies that have the most significant effect on recognised amounts — a separate note from key assumptions about estimates.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — judgments-vs-estimates disclosure split Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Estimates get assumption notes; judgments get a dedicated 'critical judgments' note. Two rooms, same corridor.
mem.link: Ch 11

questions.q: The smallest identifiable group of assets that generates cash inflows largely independent of other assets is:
questions.why: Definition of CGU (Ind AS 36). 'Reporting unit' is US-GAAP goodwill lingo, not an Ind AS 36 term.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — definition matching is the easy-half of impairment questions AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: CGU = smallest independent cash machine. If it depends on other assets for inflows, look wider.

questions.q: Under Ind AS 34, material items of income/expense in an interim period are recognised:
o: On the same recognition principles as annual FS
questions.why: Ind AS 34 uses the same recognition/measurement principles as annual reporting (discrete view) with specified aggregation/disclosure; not budget-based smoothing.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — discrete-vs-integral trap Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Interims are not mini-budgets: the same recognition laws apply, plus 34's extra disclosures.
mem.link: Ch 11

questions.q: Which is a NON-reclassifying (no recycling) OCI item?
o: Translation reserve on foreign subsidiary disposal
Financial liability FV own-credit changes (FVTPL election) AND DB remeasurements — both
questions.why: No-recycle OCI: DB remeasurements, own-credit on FVTPL-elect liabilities, and the FVOCI equity election. Translation reserve RECYCLES on disposal — the sound-alike that is not on the no-recycle roster.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the recycle roster with its famous exception AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Most OCI eventually visits P&L; the three that never check out are re-measurement, own credit, and equity-FVOCI.
mem.link: Chapter 11 — Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements

questions.q: Value in use calculations exclude:
o: Estimates of restructuring improvements NOT yet committed
questions.why: VIU: exclude income-tax cash flows, exclude financing inflows/outflows, exclude uncommitted restructuring benefits; include capex needed to maintain current condition.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).

mem.ti: TI: Ind AS 36 — cash flow exclusions
mem.tip: Pre-tax, no finance lines, no daydreams about future restructurings — the three no's of VIU.

questions.q: When a portion of a CGU containing goodwill is disposed, the goodwill included in the gain/loss is measured:
o: By relative values of the operation disposed and retained portion, unless another method better reflects the carrying
questions.why: Ind AS 36 disposal-of-portion rule: relative-value default for goodwill; no NCI adjustment — P&L on the way out.

questions.topic: Amendment — gain on loss of control (narrow-scope)
questions.q: The narrow-scope amendment to Ind AS 110/Ind AS 28 (adopted in India for annual periods beginning on/after 1 April 2025) clarifies that when an entity loses control of a subsidiary that contains a business:
o: Gain on the retained interest is not recognised
Full gain/loss is recognised on loss of control — the prohibition on remeasurement does not apply to the retained interest
questions.why: Documented narrow-scope amendment (IASB; ICAI effective per the notification for periods beginning on/after 1 April 2025): the parent recognises the FULL gain/loss arising from loss of control, including on the retained interest; the partial-disposal offset rule for associates/JVs remains. Verify the exact ICAI notification text in your study material — candidates should not treat effective dates as guaranteed.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — narrow-scope fixes often arrive just before an exam cycle — high-alert area Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.ti: TI: Amendment — gain on loss of control (narrow-scope)
mem.tip: Losing control is a full exit for tax-of-gain purposes even if you keep a seat at the table.
mem.link: Chapter 11 — Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements

questions.q: A CGU (goodwill Rs 41 lakh; identifiable assets Rs 500 lakh) has FVLCS Rs 480 lakh and value in use Rs 422 lakh. The impairment outcome is:
o: Impairment Rs 61 lakh pro rata across all assets including goodwill equally
Impairment Rs 61 lakh on VIU being lower
No impairment since FVLCS exceeds book
Impairment Rs 61 lakh: goodwill 41, other assets 20
questions.why: RA = higher of 480 and 422 = 480; CA 541 ⇒ impairment 61 lakh, absorbed by goodwill (full 41) then the balance 20 pro rata over the other assets.

questions.q: A machine (cost Rs 100 lakh, life 10 years, nil residual) was written down to Rs 45 lakh after 3 years of depreciation. In year 4, indicators reverse; what ceiling applies to the year-4 reversal (Rs lakh)?
o: Cap at original cost Rs 100 lakh
Maximum recovery of Rs 60 lakh — capped at what the CA would have been
questions.why: Ceiling = carrying amount net of depreciation that WOULD have existed had no impairment occurred: 100 − 4×10 = Rs 60 lakh. Post-impairment the year-4 CA is 45 − 4.5 = 40.5, so at most Rs 19.5 lakh can be reversed — and goodwill never reverses.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the ceiling formula (and goodwill absolute bar) is a known trap AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Ind AS 36: reversal caps at carrying amount that WOULD have existed (net of depreciation); goodwill never reverses.
